newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Bancoquia shares rise on acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Bancoquia shares rise on acquisition.

text.p: Shares in Bancoquia, Colombia's eighth largest bank in terms of assets, gained 9.48 percent on the Bogota exchange Tuesday on news that Spain's Grupo Santander was buying a controlling stake in the bank.

Bancoquia shares climbed to 5,400 pesos in a 491.7 million peso volume following the early morning joint announcement by Grupo Santander and brewing giant Bavaria, which controlled the Colombian bank.
Santander will take a 55 percent stake in Bancoquia in a $151 million deal that still has to be approved by the Spanish and Colombian authorities.

"This is a very good piece of news. This buy will make Bancoquia shares even more solid. As it is they're some of the safest shares in the market at the moment. Santander and Bancoquia is a perfect match," said one Bogota trader who did not wish to be named.
Bancoquia has 128 branches across the country. With assets of $1.39 billion, Bancoquia was the financial arm of the powerful Santo Domingo industrial congolmerate, of which Bavaria is a part.
Under the terms of the deal it will shed its holdings in investment bank Corfinorte and in warehousing company Almagran.
It will take 100 percent control of Colombia's second largest finance company Invercredito, which has assets of 325.6 billion pesos.

In the press statement, Grupo Santander chairman Emilio Botin said: "We're very satisfied with this operation. Bancoquia without doubt fits into our strategy of expansion in Latin America and shows the confidence that Santander has in the future of Colombia."
Grupo Santander's investment bank, Santander Investments has been operating in Colombia since 1994.
Midway through the year Spanish banking giant Banco Bilbao Vizcaya acquired 40 percent of Colombia's Banco Ganadero, now the country's largest in terms of assets.

After Tuesday's announcement, Bavaria chairman Augusto Lopez said: "To face stiff competition in the banking sector, a bank needs the type of solidity, solvency and prestige that characterizes the Banco Santander."
